# 07 — a disjunction

Hand-written fixture, 2026-09-13.

## Document

`assertion.sub == '…main' || assertion.sub == '…dev'`.

## Expected

`{aud="…/providers/github", sub="repo:acme/infra:ref:refs/heads/dev"} | {aud="…/providers/github", sub="repo:acme/infra:ref:refs/heads/main"}`,
exact: two Terms, in canonical order.

## Why

`||` is CEL's logical or; a credential passes when either operand holds,
which is the Join of the two sets. The lattice keeps a Join of Terms as
Terms, so this renders as two, where the same two values under `in` (case
02) render as one Term holding a union. Both are exact; they are different
canonical forms, and the harness judges by canonical form.

## Sources

- https://github.com/google/cel-spec/blob/master/doc/langdef.md (`||`)
- internal/eval/admitted.go (AdmittedSet: a union of Terms)
